title: Temporary transitional aid guarantee: half retired
note: Closes half the gap between the FY2020 baseline and the formula amount. Interacts with provision 1: a higher formula amount lifts districts off the floor before the floor is lowered.
baseline_source: uncodified:The guarantee is temporary law, carried in the uncodified sections of H.B. 33 and H.B. 96 rather than in a Revised Code section, so no committed statutory text states it.

title: Special education category weights raised 8 percent
note: No lever expresses a categorical weight. Adding one costs a field on Policy, a checkpoint in bundle, and a mirrored implementation in web/src/lib/policy.ts, or verify.ts refuses to render the scenario page.

title: Transportation reimbursement floor raised to 37.5 percent
note: Levered against project::transport::floor. The draft was written against 29.17 percent; H.B. 96 raised the floor to 50 percent after, which inverts the provision's sign — read against FY2027 law this is a reduction of 12.5 points rather than a rise. The floor is worth $289.6M statewide and its incidence runs up the wealth distribution, so a cut falls hardest on the districts with the highest local capacity.
baseline_source: statute:fifty per cent or the district's state share percentage

title: Resident district held harmless for scholarship deductions
note: Outside the model. The deduct channel needs the per-agency participation series the deduction calculator was declared for and never got.
baseline_source: superseded:as that division existed prior to September 30, 2021

title: Formula transition supplement repealed alongside the guarantee
note: Provision 2 retires half the guarantee and Section 265.225 would make 90.9 percent of that good, because the guarantee is a term in the supplement's own subtrahend. A draft that retires the guarantee without this provision is a net spend rather than a cut. Stated as its own provision so the choice is visible rather than implied by silence.
baseline_source: uncodified:The formula transition supplement is temporary law, carried in the uncodified Section 265.225 of H.B. 110 and extended to FY2026 and FY2027 by H.B. 96 in the same clause that extends the guarantee it backstops, so no committed statutory text states it.

note: Outside the model. The scholarship channel is not carried at all: the 609 districts here are the traditional districts in the department's own calculator, and a change to who may receive a voucher moves nothing any lever reaches.

title: Formula payments suspended for FY2026 and FY2027
note: Section 265.235(B). Binds no parameter: there is no value to move, only a statute switched off. R.C. 3317.022 is the phase-in interpolation, so this is what makes provision 1 a dead letter.

title: Temporary foundation funding: FY2025 aid plus half the distance
baseline: FY2020 funding base plus the phase-in fraction of the distance
proposed: FY2025 state foundation funding plus 0.50 of the distance to the computed amount, floored at zero
note: Section 265.235(C)-(D). The same interpolation R.C. 3317.022 performs, from a different base: FY2025 actual aid rather than the FY2020 funding base. That base is not a lever position and is not in DistrictRecord, which is why the whole stage is unpriceable here.
baseline_source: uncodified:Section 265.235 is temporary law in the House-passed substitute and was not enacted, so it appears in no committed statutory text.

title: Enrollment growth supplement, banded by growth rate
baseline: no enrollment growth supplement in FY2025
proposed: nothing below 3 percent growth, then $150/$100/$50 per enrolled pupil in FY2026 and $200/$150/$100 in FY2027
note: Section 265.235(E). The rate falls as growth rises, so a district growing 11 percent receives a third of the per-pupil rate of one growing 4 percent. No lever expresses a banded per-pupil grant.
baseline_source: uncodified:Section 265.235 is temporary law in the House-passed substitute and was not enacted, so it appears in no committed statutory text.

title: Base funding supplement, $20 then $30 a pupil

note: Section 265.235(F), to every traditional district, JVSD, community and STEM school. Priceable arithmetic with no lever to carry it.
